A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AoPS-Instruct and LiveAoPSBench work. Their main text, tables, figures, mathematical examples, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, human validation, and rewriting and computation-budget ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds temporal-overlap measurements, a DART-Math-Hard comparison, and complete-2024 benchmark evaluations.

M1.justification: The extraction and rewriting pipeline, decontamination rules, answer cross-checking, and proposed fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The appendix prompts are also retained; newly evaluated models and training corpora do not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Table 9 adds actual fine-tuning on DART-Math-Hard, expanding training-data coverage with another math instruction corpus. Existing evaluation tasks remain, including AIME24 and AMC23, whose main comparison moves to appendix Table 8.

E2.justification: Table 9 introduces DART-Math-Hard as a directly evaluated alternative to AoPS-Instruct. The new full-year comparison in Figure 8 substantially expands the evaluated model roster with QwQ-32B-Preview, four DeepSeek-R1-distilled variants, and Phi-4. Earlier Numina and model comparisons remain available.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds evaluation on 5,328 January–December 2024 questions alongside the retained 3,863-question January–August set. Section 4.2 introduces four-month bins for measuring 10-gram overlap with Numina. The stated three-epoch fine-tuning and 386-case human-validation designs are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 2 add a direct analysis of whether newer questions overlap less with Numina training data. Existing rewriting and computation-budget ablations, benchmark correlation, difficulty and answer-type breakdowns, and qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: v1 explains and reports 91% inter-annotator agreement; v2 removes that calculation description and result, although Section 3.2 still says agreement is reported. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty estimates or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds temporal-overlap results, DART comparison scores, and full-year model curves. Existing scores also change: AoPS-trained DeepSeek-Math moves from 20.1 to 19.0 on LiveAoPSBench, 62.3 to 58.8 on MATH, and 22.4 to 24.3 on OlympiadBench (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). Several Llama-3.2-3B and AIME/AMC entries change too. Human-validation outcomes change from 88/8/4% to 92/5/3% for correct/incorrect/no-answer. These are reported revisions, without an explanation establishing reruns.

T1.justification: No theoretical framework, formal assumption, theorem, or proof is added or revised. The mathematical solution examples and their reasoning remain unchanged apart from typesetting and figure renumbering.

C1.justification: The central claims about automated curation, contamination-resistant evaluation, and fine-tuning benefits remain. The introduction revises the claimed dataset size from 666.1K to 652K QA pairs and explicitly states that LiveAoPSBench stays regularly updated; the abstract and conclusion otherwise retain their scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explicit argument using 91% human agreement to contextualize imperfect answer validation. It adds discussion interpreting temporal Numina overlap as support for timestamp-based contamination mitigation. The limitations concerning visual content, proof evaluation, and community-content quality, together with appendix failure examples, remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that fine-tuning uses the full decontaminated corpora: 824K Numina and 647K AoPS-Instruct pairs. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed training settings. Access directions change from the original repository to a leaderboard site, also referenced for updated results.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to DART-Math, ScaleQuest, MATH2, DeepSeek-R1, and QwQ. Table 1 adds DART-Math and the already-cited MAmmoTH2. These update the surrounding literature without substantially redefining the work's positioning relative to Numina, Omni-MATH, or contamination-resistant benchmarks.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative order are retained. Targeted additions include Section 4.2, Appendix B.1, an appendix section for relocated AIME/AMC results, an impact statement, and acknowledgments, alongside limited wording and header edits.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 4 changes from a two-by-two arrangement to one row, and Figure 5's panels become vertically stacked. v1 Table 2 is split between v2 Tables 3 and 8. New displays include the overlap table, full-year model plot, and DART comparison.

improvement.justification: The temporal-overlap analysis, additional training-corpus comparison, and complete-2024 reasoning-model evaluations modestly strengthen empirical support and benchmark relevance. Reporting weaknesses limit the gain: existing scores and validation percentages change without explanation, and the 91% agreement result disappears. Table 2 also contains an intermediate increase despite describing a consistent decrease. The additions improve the evidence without resolving the paper's main methodological limitations.
